## Summary

**Refactor dense forensic tables**

Identity and control-plane tables use many tiny columns and repeated metadata.

## Priority / wave

- Priority: **P2**
- Wave: **V3**
- Complexity: **L**
- Audit code: `UX-P2-02`
- DUX code: `DUX5-21`

## Scope

Trust and Run Explorer.

Screenshot groups: SG-01, SG-07 dense tables

## Concrete change

Present top 4–6 operator columns; move raw fields to explorer drawer/JSON artifact; add column priority rules.

## Expected effect

Tables remain readable without deleting evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Table cell text meets minimum; no horizontal clipping at 1366; full evidence accessible via drill-down.
- Aligns with epic acceptance: Status/Reason/Impact/Action visible without internal scroll on first viewport
- No new high-cardinality Prometheus labels
- No hidden verdict logic introduced only in Grafana transforms

## Dependencies

Dedicated explorer or table plugin capabilities.

## Risk

May require control-plane endpoint projection, but must remain interface/application owned.

## Overlap / predecessor notes

Table projection residual after DUX4-25.

## Constraints

- Surgical dashboard JSON only; preserve panel IDs where possible
- Run Explorer remains forensic owner when moving detail off domain boards
- Prefer description/runbook for caveats; keep first-screen copy to 2-4 lines
- Tech-debt budgets non-increasing

## Verification

- [ ] Before/after screenshots for affected panels (dark theme)
- [ ] Viewports: 1366x768, 1440x900, 1920x1080 at 100% (125% when layout-sensitive)
- [ ] Targeted pytest for navigation/contracts if JSON structure changes
- [ ] Manual operator 5-second comprehension check on first-screen card

DUX5 epic (#7116)
